questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Following the alarming data breach, the cybersecurity
team investigated thoroughly the suspicious activity
detected within the encrypted servers.
No Error
options_hi: Following the alarming data breach, the cybersecurity
team investigated thoroughly the suspicious activity
detected within the encrypted servers.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “investigated thoroughly the” with “investigated the suspicious activity thoroughly”.

Rule / Concept: Position of Adverb of Manner

An Adverb of Manner (which answers the question "How?") should generally be placed after the intransitive verb or after the direct object. Crucially, an adverb should never be placed between a transitive verb and its direct object.

Position of adverb of manner

Intransitive verbs:- After the main verb

Transitive verbs:- After the object ( If object is small.)

Transitive verbs:- Before the main verb

(If object is a noun clause.)

Application to the Given Question

"...the cybersecurity team investigated thoroughly the suspicious activity..."

In this sentence, "investigated" is a transitive verb and "the suspicious activity" is its direct object. Placing the adverb "thoroughly" between the verb and the object disrupts the flow of the sentence. The adverb must either come before the verb or, more commonly in exam patterns, after the entire object.

Corrected Sentence

Following the alarming data breach, the cybersecurity team investigated the suspicious activity thoroughly within the encrypted servers. (Alternatively: "...thoroughly investigated the suspicious activity...")

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1: She speaks English well. (Verb + Object + Adverb) ✅

Example 2: He ate the chocolate greedily. (Verb + Object + Adverb) ✅

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1: She speaks well English. ❌

Wrong example 2: He ate greedily the chocolate. ❌

hings to Remember / Exam Tips

  • Spotting the Object: Always identify if the verb has an object. If you see "Verb + Adverb + Noun," check if that noun is the object of the verb. If it is, the adverb is likely misplaced.

  • Intransitive Exception: If there is no object, the adverb immediately follows the verb (e.g., "He walked slowly").

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Whenever the eccentric professor begins his
lecture with a series of unintentional puns,
we cannot help but to laugh at him.
options_hi: Whenever the eccentric professor begins his
lecture with a series of unintentional puns,
we cannot help but to laugh at him.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “to laugh” with “laugh”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Bare Infinitives after "Cannot help but"

the structure "Cannot help but" is a fixed idiomatic expression. The "but" in this phrase functions similarly to "except." When this specific combination is used, it must be followed by a Bare Infinitive (V1 without "to").

It is crucial to distinguish this from the phrase "Cannot help" (without the "but"), which requires a Gerund (V{ing}).

  • Structure 1: Cannot help + V{ing} (e.g., I cannot help laughing.)

  • Structure 2: Cannot help but + V1 (e.g., I cannot help but laugh.)



💢 Application to the Given Question

"...we cannot help but to laugh at him."

In this sentence, the phrase "cannot help but" is used. Following the rules of this idiomatic construction, the verb that follows must be in its base form (V1). The inclusion of "to" before "laugh" creates a full infinitive, which is grammatically incorrect in this specific context.

Corrected Sentence

Whenever the eccentric professor begins his lecture with a series of unintentional puns, we cannot help but laugh at him.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The heritage committee finally approved the proposal to exhibit a remarkably preserved,
after years of careful restoration and expert conservation under international supervision,
ancient Egyptian ceremonial metal mask that had remained inaccessible to the public for decades.
options_hi: The heritage committee finally approved the proposal to exhibit a remarkably preserved,
after years of careful restoration and expert conservation under international supervision,
ancient Egyptian ceremonial metal mask that had remained inaccessible to the public for decades.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C).

Replace “ancient Egyptian ceremonial metal” with “ancient Egyptian metal ceremonial”.

Rule / Concept: OSASCOMP (Order of Adjectives)

When more than one adjective is used before a noun, they must follow a fixed sequence:

Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color → Origin → Material → Purpose.

Any deviation from this order results in a grammatical error, even though each adjective is individually correct.

Application to the Given Question - “ancient Egyptian ceremonial metal mask”.

Classification of adjectives:

ancient → Age

Egyptian → Origin

metal → Material

ceremonial → Purpose

As per OSASCOMP, Material must come before Purpose, but here ceremonial (Purpose) is incorrectly placed before metal (Material).

Corrected Sentence - The heritage committee finally approved the proposal to exhibit a remarkably preserved, after years of careful restoration and expert conservation under international supervision, ancient Egyptian metal ceremonial mask that had remained inaccessible to the public for decades.

More Examples for Clarity -

a beautiful Italian leather handbag.

an old Indian wooden temple door.

a modern German steel medical instrument.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Always identify the function of each adjective before checking order.

Material vs Purpose errors are highly tested in SSC CGL Mains.

Long sentences are designed to distract—focus only on adjective sequencing.

questions.q_en:
Transparency is widely regarded as a cornerstone of democratic governance, yet its practical implementation often proves challenging. Governments may publicly endorse openness, but administrative processes frequently remain [---1---], limiting citizens’ ability to scrutinize decision-making. In some cases, excessive procedural complexity serves to [---2---] accountability rather than enhance it, creating a gap between formal disclosure and meaningful access to information. Such practices can foster public [---3---], as repeated assurances of openness fail to translate into tangible outcomes. Consequently, experts argue that transparency must be treated not as a symbolic gesture but as a [---4---] commitment embedded within institutional culture.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :

Such practices can foster public [---3---], as repeated assurances of openness fail to translate into tangible outcomes. Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :

opaque
participatory

opaque

questions.solution_en:

• Accessible suggests ease of scrutiny, which contradicts the limitation described.
• Participatory implies active citizen involvement, not secrecy.
• Streamlined refers to efficiency, not lack of clarity.

options_en: After missing the last bus home, the weary
travelers were none too pleased to find
that the only nearby hotel was fully booked.
No Error
options_hi: After missing the last bus home, the weary
travelers were none too pleased to find
that the only nearby hotel was fully booked.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D) No Error.

Rule / Concept: "None too" as a Qualifier

The phrase "none too" is an idiomatic expression that means "not very" or "not particularly." It is used to indicate that a quality is present only in a small or unsatisfactory amount

ONLY TOO (very) NONE TOO(not very)

Application to the Given Question

"After missing the last bus home, the weary travelers were none too pleased to find that the only nearby hotel was fully booked."

Let's break down the logic:

  1. The Situation: The travelers missed their bus (bad luck) and found the hotel was full (more bad luck).

  2. The Emotion: In this situation, a person would not be very pleased.

  3. The Phrase: "None too pleased" perfectly captures this sentiment of being "not very happy" or "quite unhappy."

Since the phrase is used correctly to show a lack of pleasure in a frustrating situation, there is no grammatical error.

More Examples for Clarity

  • None too (= Not very): The service at the restaurant was none too fast. (It was slow/unsatisfactory). ✅

  • Only too (= Very): I am only too aware of the difficulties ahead. (I am very/painfully aware). ✅

questions.q_en:
Identify the type of the highlighted clause.

The players who practiced consistently throughout the season performed exceptionally well during the final tournament.
questions.q_hi:
Identify the type of the highlighted clause.

The players who practiced consistently throughout the season performed exceptionally well during the final tournament.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: B) Adjective Clause

Explanation: An adjective clause modifies a noun or pronoun and usually begins with a relative pronoun such as who, which, or that.

The highlighted clause:

“who practiced consistently throughout the season” describes the noun “players.”

Which players? → players who practiced consistently throughout the season

Therefore, it is an adjective clause.

Why other options are incorrect:

A) A noun clause functions as a noun, not as a modifier.

C) An adverb clause modifies verbs/adjectives/adverbs.

D) A main clause can stand independently, whereas this clause depends on the main sentence.

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “listened to” with “heard”

📌 Rule / Concept: Hear vs. Listen to –

Both verbs relate to the sense of hearing, but they differ based on intent and effort:

Hear: To perceive sound through the ears physically. It is an involuntary action that happens regardless of whether you want it to (e.g., "I heard a loud bang").

Listen to: To pay attention to a sound. It is a voluntary/intentional action where you make an effort to understand or enjoy what is being heard (e.g., "I am listening to music").

💢 Application to the Given Question - A "crash" is an accidental and sudden noise. You do not usually wait or pay attention to hear a crash; it simply happens and your ears perceive it. Since the action was sudden and unintentional, the verb heard is the correct choice. You cannot "listen" to something you didn't know was going to happen.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1 I was just walking down the street when I heard an explosion.

Example 2: Please listen to what the teacher is saying. Example 3: Can you hear me now? (Checking physical perception.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

Boy and girl each _______ present at the venue today to participate in the seminar.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

Boy and girl each _______ present at the venue today to participate in the seminar.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (D)- The blank should be filled with the plural present tense verb "are"

Logic Breakdown:

The Subject: "Boy and girl" joined by "and" creates a plural subject.

The Position of "Each": Because "each" appears after the nouns, the plural agreement is maintained.

Tense Consistency: The word "today" indicates the Present Tense.

Why (B) "is" is incorrect: While "is" is present tense, it is singular. The placement of "each" after the subject prevents the sentence from becoming singular.

Why (A) and (C) are eliminated: Both "was" and "were" are past tense forms and contradict the current time marker "today."

Correct Sentence: Boy and girl each are present at the venue today...

The "Each" Location Check:

Before Subject: 1.Each boy and girl is...

Before Subject: 2.Each boy and each girl is…

After Subject: Boy and girl each are...

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

As the investigation progressed, the authorities began to __________ the prime suspect.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

As the investigation progressed, the authorities began to __________ the prime suspect.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (3).

English Explanation: “Close in on” means to move nearer to someone or something in order to surround, capture, or approach it closely. It can also be used metaphorically for pressure or deadlines approaching. In the sentence, as the investigation progressed, the authorities were moving nearer to the prime suspect, possibly to surround or apprehend him. Therefore, “close in on” correctly conveys the idea of gradually approaching or tightening around someone. “Close up” means to shut something or become temporarily unavailable. “Close out” means to end or finish something, especially an account or business. “Close down” means to permanently stop operations. Since the context refers to authorities approaching a suspect, “close in on” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Close up (बंद करना / अस्थायी रूप से बंद होना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ को बंद करना।
Example: The shop closed up early due to heavy rain. (भारी बारिश के कारण दुकान जल्दी बंद हो गई।)

2. Close out (समाप्त करना / निपटाना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी खाते या कार्य को पूरी तरह समाप्त करना।
Example: The company decided to close out the old accounts. (कंपनी ने पुराने खातों को बंद करने का निर्णय लिया।)

3. Close in on (करीब पहुँचकर घेरना / दबाव बढ़ना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी के पास जाकर उसे घेर लेना या दबाव का पास आना।
Example 1: As the deadline approached, pressure began to close in on the candidates. (समयसीमा नज़दीक आने पर उम्मीदवारों पर दबाव बढ़ने लगा।)
Example 2: The police closed in on the criminal after a long chase. (लंबे पीछा करने के बाद पुलिस अपराधी के करीब पहुँच गई।)

4. Close down (स्थायी रूप से बंद करना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी संस्था या व्यवसाय को हमेशा के लिए बंद कर देना।
Example: The factory was closed down due to heavy losses. (भारी घाटे के कारण फैक्ट्री बंद कर दी गई।)

Rule / Concept: Reflexive Pronouns with Transitive Verbs -

Certain verbs in English are "reflexive" when they don't have a separate direct object. This means the action of the verb must reflect back onto the subject.

The most important verbs for exams in this category are: Absent, Avail, Enjoy, Resign, Apply, Exert, Acquit, Reconcile.

In this sentence, the verb "absent" is used as a verb (meaning to keep oneself away). When "absent" is used as a verb, it is a transitive verb that requires an object. Since there is no other person or thing being "absented," the subject (you) must perform the action upon yourself. Without the reflexive pronoun "yourself," the sentence is grammatically incomplete.

Things to Remember/Exam Tips -

Example: We enjoyed the movie. (Correct - No reflexive needed).

Example: We enjoyed ourselves. (Correct - Reflexive needed because there's no other object).

Verb vs. Adjective: Don't confuse the verb "absent" with the adjective "absent."

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Provided that the weather will remain
clear tomorrow morning, the hikers will
attempt to reach the summit of the peak.
options_hi: Provided that the weather will remain
clear tomorrow morning, the hikers will
attempt to reach the summit of the peak.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “will remain” with “remains”.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Conditional Clause Restriction

In a First Conditional sentence (which talks about real or possible future events), the sentence is divided into two parts:

  1. The Condition (The "If/Provided that" part): Must be in Simple Present Tense (V1/V{s/es}).

  2. The Result (The "Will" part): Must be in Simple Future Tense (will + V1).

Even though the "weather remaining clear" is something that will happen in the future, the conjunction "Provided that" (which works just like "If") locks the verb into the Present Tense.

💢 Application to the Question

"Provided that the weather will remain clear tomorrow... the hikers will attempt..."

  • The Error: Using "will" twice. You cannot have "will" in the conditional clause and the main clause simultaneously.

  • The Logic: The condition "weather remains clear" is treated as a present requirement for the future action "will attempt" to happen.

  • The Subject: Since "the weather" is an uncountable/singular noun, we use the singular verb form "remains."

Corrected Sentence

Provided that the weather remains clear tomorrow morning, the hikers will attempt to reach the summit of the peak.

🧠 Exam Tip: The "Future Conjunction" List

Whenever you see these words, scan the verb immediately following them. If it has a "will" or "shall," it's almost certainly an error:

  • If / Provided that / Supposing

  • When / As soon as / Before / After

  • Until / Unless / In case

📌 Rule / Concept: “Used to” Structure in Question Tags

When “used to” expresses a past habit, it behaves like a simple past structure, not like a modal verb.

Therefore, the question tag must use: did / didn’t + subject

💢 Application to the Given Question -

She used to handle the arbitration cases independently

This describes a past habit.

So, the correct tag must use didn’t, because:

  • Tense = Past

  • Auxiliary needed = did

  • Subject = she

Hence: didn’t she?

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ - He used to work late hours, didn’t he?

Example 2 ✅ - They used to travel frequently, didn’t they?

Example 3 ✅ - The firm used to outsource its legal work, didn’t it?

🧠 Things to Remember

  • “Used to” = past habit → use didn’t in tag.

  • Treat it like simple past for tag formation.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

During the charity event, the organizers decided to __________ free blankets to the homeless.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

During the charity event, the organizers decided to __________ free blankets to the homeless.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (2).

English Explanation: “Give away” means to distribute something for free or to donate something to others. In the sentence, the organizers are distributing free blankets during a charity event. Therefore, “give away” correctly conveys the idea of donating or handing out something without taking payment. “Give in” means to surrender or yield. “Give off” means to emit something like smell, light, or heat. “Give up” means to quit or stop doing something. Since the context is about distributing blankets for free, “give away” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Give in (हार मान लेना)

Example: After hours of argument, he finally gave in. (कई घंटों की बहस के बाद वह आखिरकार मान गया।)

2. Give away (मुफ्त में बाँटना / दान करना)

Example 1: The company gave away free samples to customers. (कंपनी ने ग्राहकों को मुफ्त सैंपल बाँटे।)

Example 2: She gave away her old clothes to the needy. (उसने अपने पुराने कपड़े जरूरतमंदों को दे दिए।)

3. Give off (छोड़ना / उत्सर्जित करना)

Example: The flowers give off a pleasant fragrance. (फूल सुगंध छोड़ते हैं।)

4. Give up (छोड़ देना / त्याग देना)

Example: He gave up smoking last year. (उसने पिछले साल धूम्रपान छोड़ दिया।)

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: According to the latest census data, there are
just a dozen families left in the valley who still
practice the ancient traditional art of silk weaving.
options_hi: According to the latest census data, there are
just a dozen families left in the valley who still
practice the ancient traditional art of silk weaving.
questions.solution_en:
Replace “a” with “one”.

Rule / Concept: Use of "One" with Limiters (Only, Just, Over, Exactly) –

In general English, "a" and "one" are often interchangeable when referring to a single unit (e.g., a hundred or one hundred). However, in formal grammar and competitive exams, when a number is preceded by specific limiters like Only, Just, Over, Under, Exactly, or Approximately, we must use "one" instead of the indefinite article "a/an." This is because these limiters serve to emphasize a precise quantity or a specific limit, and "one" carries more numerical weight and precision than the generic "a."

Corrected Sentence- According to the latest census data, there are just one dozen families left in the valley who still practice the ancient traditional art of silk weaving.

More Examples for Clarity-

1. I have only one hundred rupees left in my wallet.

2. It took over one hour to clear the security check.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips-

The "Emphasis" Key: If you see words that restrict or specify a number (Only/Just/Over), your "Grammar Radar" should immediately look for "one."

A vs. One: Use "a" for general statements (e.g., "A hundred people attended"). Use "one" for precision or when limiters are present.

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C).

Replace “could not speak both” with “could speak neither”.

📌 Rule / Concept: "Both" in Negative Sentences

The word both is used to emphasize the inclusion of two people or things in an affirmative (positive) statement. However, both should never be used with a negative verb (not) to mean "none of the two."

When you want to say "not the first one AND not the second one," the correct construction is to use neither with a positive verb. Using "both... not" is considered a grammatical error in competitive exams because it creates logical ambiguity.

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1: Both of them are not going to the party. ❌

Wrong example 2: I do not have both the books you asked for. ❌

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: Neither of the two brothers is honest. ✅ (Instead of: Both brothers are not honest.)

Example 2: I like neither tea nor coffee. ✅ (Instead of: I do not like both tea and coffee.)
